judged_text: refreshOAuthTokens POSTs calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header, signature, or shared secret, so the sync endpoint can only hand out a user's OAuth access tokens to unauthenticated callers. Anyone who can reach the configured sync endpoint (e.g. an internet-reachable sync route on the parent cal.com deployment) can POST calcomUserId=<n> for arbitrary n and receive that user's fresh access token, harvesting credentials across all users by id enumeration; the diff's own webhook direction authenticates with a shared-secret header, but this direction sends nothing the endpoint could authenticate.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Cal.com will `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth header/signature/secret. The diff does show inbound webhook auth via `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` header checking (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), but there is no analogous mechanism for the outbound token-refresh sync call. However, the finding’s claim that “anyone who can reach the configured sync endpoint can POST ... and receive tokens” depends on how that external endpoint is implemented/exposed, which is not shown in the diff; what is verifiable is that this client provides no built-in authentication material to let the endpoint verify the caller.
